name: upgrade-body-current-code
body:
source: spine-backfill/feedback-5 on solution.component.upgrade — the body still read as a plan ("Owned by an `internal/cli` handler (a new `upgrade` case in cli.Run …) plus a new `internal/scaffold` upgrade entry point"), but both already exist: cli.Run dispatches the `upgrade` case to runUpgrade (internal/cli/cli.go:96, internal/cli/upgrade.go:54) and internal/scaffold's upgrade/refresh/migrate/catalog halves exist (internal/scaffold/upgrade.go, refresh.go, migrate.go, catalog.go with its embedded scaffoldversions.json).

before: "...Owned by an `internal/cli` handler (a new `upgrade` case in cli.Run, beside init, init-library, start, templates, version and help) plus a new `internal/scaffold` upgrade entry point; it reuses the embedded author guides and init seed content and the template library loader and deck loader for validation, writes nothing unless it is safe, and is local-filesystem only with no `--force`."

after: present-tense description of the current code — runUpgrade (no argument, no `--force`, os.Getwd, exit codes 0/1/2), cli.Run's `upgrade` dispatch (that shared dispatcher is owned by solution.component.cli-commands), and scaffold.Upgrade's orchestration of detectProject / checkSupportedLibraryFormat / refreshScaffold (refreshMember, writeMember, detectSeedDeck) / migrateLibrary → runMigrations over registeredMigrations, the embedded digest catalogue in catalog.go (catalogLookup), end-to-end validation and the all-or-nothing undo.

Resolution [autonomous]: rewrote solution.component.upgrade's body in the present tense and dropped the forward-looking "new …" wording; no edge changes — the component's implemented-by anchors already cover runUpgrade and the four internal/scaffold files, and the cli.Run dispatch case belongs to solution.component.cli-commands (per solution.note.spine-backfill-reconcile), so it is named in prose, not re-owned here.
